title: Doubled Midpoint Of Two Ledgers
description:
## Task

Two ledgers are each sorted. Imagine merging them into one sorted list and taking its median. To avoid fractions, return the median doubled: the sum of the two middle values if the merged length is even, or twice the middle value if it is odd. Do it in O(log(min(n, m))) time by binary searching how many entries of the shorter ledger fall in the lower half of the merge, not by merging.

## Input

- `a`, `b` — lists of integers, each sorted in non-decreasing order. At least one of them is non-empty.

## Output

The doubled median of all values in `a` and `b` combined, as an integer.

## Example

```python
doubled_midpoint([1, 3], [2])  # returns 4
doubled_midpoint([1, 2], [3, 4])  # returns 5
doubled_midpoint([], [5])  # returns 10
```

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ length of `a` + length of `b` ≤ 4·10^5
- -10^9 ≤ each value ≤ 10^9
signature: def doubled_midpoint(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> int
